 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Amazon earnings: Capex and cash flow dent AMZN shares, but AWS might be a $1T business . 

 Incoming! New Jersey governor weighs options to block Russian diesel cargoes . 

 Remix: Spotify ( SPOT ) targets launch of AI music service early next year.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Trick or treat 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 The digital asset world is reeling after a devastating cyberattack. A hack on the world's largest crypto exchange, Binance, has compromised $6.3B of funds , prompting the company to temporarily suspend withdrawals as it investigates the incident. The company is working with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with about $3B frozen on-chain so far, but that doesn't mean they will be recovered (barring stablecoins where the issuer controls the token contract).

 Who was behind it? "The attack [is linked] to TraderTraitor, North Korea's elite hacking unit , based on robust on and off-chain intelligence," according to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs. "We make this judgment with high confidence." Hackers appear to have exploited the transaction process of Binance by gaining access to internal systems via a DevOps engineer's laptop, and authorized transfers across 10 different blockchains.

There's worry in the industry that the massive hack could send the crypto world into a bear market, similar to the loss in confidence after past damaging events at FTX and Mt. Gox. Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) fell 5% to below $77,000 on the news, sliding to its lowest level since September, while other tokens, like Ethereum ( ETH-USD ) and Ripple ( XRP-USD ), also sold off. Increased volatility can take place in the coming days, especially if it looks like there will be fresh congressional scrutiny of the crypto industry following midterm elections.

 What's next? Binance said all "user funds are safe" and it will cover all losses, seemingly from operational reserves, future earnings, and emergency funds. "The reported scale of the incident is certainly alarming," said Yuya Hasegawa, market analyst at cryptocurrency exchange Bitbank. "That said, if Binance can demonstrate that customer assets remain secure, cover any losses, and restore normal operations promptly, the market impact could prove relatively short-lived. Bitcoin's underlying fundamentals have not been directly compromised by this incident." ( 7 comments )

Featured
 
 
 
 Free Webinar: Year-End Rally Watch - Fundamentals vs. FOMO 
 
 
 
 
 
 When stocks start climbing, the fear of missing out can be hard to ignore. And with midterm election years historically associated with strong year-end market performance, investors may be wondering whether another rally is on the horizon.

 But a rising market doesn't mean every stock is worth buying. How can you tell when momentum is supported by solid fundamentals, and when excitement is pushing prices beyond what the numbers justify?

 Join Steven Cress, VP of Quantitative Strategy at Seeking Alpha, on November 2 at 4 PM ET for a free live webinar on navigating a potential year-end rally without getting caught up in the hype.

 Steven will explore historical market patterns, the risks of chasing momentum, and how a data-driven approach can help investors stay focused on earnings, profitability, and valuation rather than market sentiment alone.
 

 Bring your questions for the live Q&A.
